label: Athletes
rubric: Current form/ranking · Career achievements · Marketability/fame · Big-moment reputation
note: This category goes stale fastest. Ratings reflect standing as of mid-2026 and should be refreshed periodically, especially for currently-active athletes.

entries.name: Michael Jordan
entries.rationale: Six titles, six Finals MVPs, and the global template for athlete marketability.

entries.name: Lionel Messi
entries.rationale: Record Ballon d'Or haul capped by a World Cup, settling most GOAT arguments.

entries.name: Muhammad Ali
entries.rationale: Transcended sport entirely; arguably the most famous athlete who ever lived.

entries.name: LeBron James
entries.rationale: All-time scoring leader with titles across three franchises and unmatched longevity.

entries.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
entries.rationale: Five Ballon d'Ors, a record Champions League scoring mark, and colossal global reach.

entries.name: Pelé
entries.rationale: Three World Cups and the original global face of football.

entries.name: Wayne Gretzky
entries.rationale: Holds hockey records so far ahead of the field they may never be approached.

entries.name: Serena Williams
entries.rationale: 23 major singles titles and a defining cultural presence well beyond tennis.

entries.name: Tom Brady
entries.rationale: Seven Super Bowl rings, more than any single franchise has won.

entries.name: Novak Djokovic
entries.rationale: Leads the all-time major count with the most complete résumé in men's tennis.

entries.name: Michael Phelps
entries.rationale: The most decorated Olympian in history by a wide margin.

entries.name: Diego Maradona
entries.rationale: Carried a nation to a World Cup almost single-handedly; mythic status.

entries.name: Usain Bolt
entries.rationale: Still holds the 100m and 200m world records with unmatched showmanship.

entries.name: Roger Federer
entries.rationale: 20 majors and perhaps the most universally admired athlete of his era.

entries.name: Rafael Nadal
entries.rationale: 22 majors including an absurd clay-court record that defines dominance.

entries.name: Simone Biles
entries.rationale: Most decorated gymnast ever, with skills literally named after her.

entries.name: Kobe Bryant
entries.rationale: Five titles and a competitive reputation that became its own cultural shorthand.

entries.name: Babe Ruth
entries.rationale: Reshaped baseball itself and remains its most mythologized figure.

entries.name: Tiger Woods
entries.rationale: 15 majors and single-handedly transformed golf's audience and economics.

entries.name: Ayrton Senna
entries.rationale: Three titles and a legend in motorsport that only grew after his death.

entries.name: Shohei Ohtani
entries.rationale: Two-way dominance unseen in a century, plus enormous international pull.

entries.name: Stephen Curry
entries.rationale: Rewrote how basketball is played; the greatest shooter ever.

entries.name: Lewis Hamilton
entries.rationale: Seven world titles and the most race wins in Formula 1 history.

entries.name: Magic Johnson
entries.rationale: Five titles and one half of the rivalry that saved the NBA.

entries.name: Jackie Robinson
entries.rationale: Historic significance that extends far past his considerable on-field record.

entries.name: Kylian Mbappé
entries.rationale: A World Cup winner in his teens and the sport's defining current attacker.

entries.name: Patrick Mahomes
entries.rationale: Multiple Super Bowl wins and MVPs before turning 30.

entries.name: Max Verstappen
entries.rationale: A dominant run of consecutive championships in a hugely competitive era.

entries.name: Jesse Owens
entries.rationale: Four golds in 1936 with historical resonance far beyond athletics.

entries.name: Shaquille O'Neal
entries.rationale: The most physically unstoppable center ever, plus huge post-career fame.

entries.name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
entries.rationale: Two MVPs, a title, and a Finals performance for the ages.

entries.name: Nikola Jokić
entries.rationale: Multiple MVPs and a championship as the game's most unusual superstar.

entries.name: Carl Lewis
entries.rationale: Nine Olympic golds across four Games in sprints and long jump.

entries.name: Katie Ledecky
entries.rationale: Long-distance swimming dominance with a stack of world records.

entries.name: Larry Bird
entries.rationale: Three MVPs, three titles, and a legendary clutch reputation.

entries.name: Erling Haaland
entries.rationale: Scoring at a historically absurd rate, though still building his trophy case.

entries.name: Kevin Durant
entries.rationale: One of the purest scorers ever with two Finals MVPs and Olympic golds.

entries.name: Connor McDavid
entries.rationale: The most dominant individual talent in current hockey by consensus.

entries.name: Jon Jones
entries.rationale: Widely rated the greatest MMA fighter ever, with a controversial off-cage record.

entries.name: Sidney Crosby
entries.rationale: Three Stanley Cups plus an Olympic golden goal that defined a generation.

entries.name: Allyson Felix
entries.rationale: The most decorated American track athlete in Olympic history.

entries.name: Luka Dončić
entries.rationale: Elite offensive production and playoff heroics, still chasing a title.

entries.name: Kevin De Bruyne
entries.rationale: The definitive creative midfielder of his era with a full trophy cabinet.

entries.name: Mohamed Salah
entries.rationale: Prolific goalscorer, Champions League winner, and a continental icon.

entries.name: Aaron Judge
entries.rationale: MVP-level power hitting with a record-setting home run season.

entries.name: Mia Hamm
entries.rationale: Set the standard for women's football globally and drove its commercial growth.

entries.name: Neymar
entries.rationale: Extraordinary technical talent and fame, but a trophy record short of the top tier.

entries.name: Conor McGregor
entries.rationale: The biggest draw combat sports has ever had, though his competitive peak has passed.

entries.name: Megan Rapinoe
entries.rationale: World Cup winner and Ballon d'Or recipient with a large cultural footprint.

entries.name: Alex Morgan
entries.rationale: Two World Cup titles and one of the sport's most marketable names.
